---
title: "Code coverage"
description: "Use Bun's built-in code coverage reporting to track test coverage and find untested code"
---

Bun's test runner has built-in code coverage reporting. Use it to see how much of your codebase your tests cover and to find untested code.

## Enabling Coverage

`bun test` reports which functions, lines, statements and branches your tests cover. Pass `--coverage` to print a coverage report to the console:

```bash terminal icon="terminal"
bun test --coverage

--------------|---------|---------|---------|----------|-------------------
File          | % Funcs | % Lines | % Stmts | % Branch | Uncovered Line #s
--------------|---------|---------|---------|----------|-------------------
All files     |   83.33 |   91.80 |   90.00 |    75.00 |
 src/api.ts   |   75.00 |   85.71 |   83.33 |    70.00 | 15-18,25
 src/main.ts  |  100.00 |  100.00 |  100.00 |    75.00 | 12
 src/utils.ts |  100.00 |  100.00 |  100.00 |   100.00 |
--------------|---------|---------|---------|----------|-------------------
```

### Enable by Default

To enable coverage reporting by default, add this to your `bunfig.toml`:

```toml title="bunfig.toml"
[test]
# Always enable coverage
coverage = true
```

### Report Files That No Test Loads

By default, the report lists the files in the working directory that your tests load. To list a fixed set of files, set `coverageInclude`. A file that matches and is never loaded counts as not covered. Bun reads it without running it.

```toml title="bunfig.toml" icon="settings"
[test]
coverageInclude = ["src/**/*.{ts,tsx}", "!src/generated"]
```

```bash terminal icon="terminal"
# Or via CLI
bun test --coverage-include="src/**/*.{ts,tsx}" --coverage-include="!src/generated"
```

Each entry is a glob pattern, a folder or a file, relative to the working directory. A pattern can end in the name of a folder, like `packages/*/src`, and it can lead out of the working directory, like `../shared`. An entry that starts with `!` excludes files, wherever it is in the list. Wildcards don't follow symlinks and don't look for files in `coverageDir`. A file that takes a [plugin](/runtime/plugins) to load, such as `.svelte`, is listed only if a test loads it. This option corresponds to Jest's `collectCoverageFrom` and Vitest's `coverage.include`.

### Report Changed Files

With `--changed`, the report lists the files that changed and the files that a changed test file imports. Thresholds apply to those files.

```bash terminal icon="terminal"
bun test --coverage --changed=main
```

## What Counts as Covered

Bun measures the code as you wrote it. Types, `import` statements, `export { … }` lists and code that the transpiler generates are not part of the report.

| Metric     | Covered when                    |
| ---------- | ------------------------------- |
| Functions  | The body of the function starts |
| Lines      | Any code on the line runs       |
| Statements | The statement starts            |
| Branches   | The code goes that way          |

### Branches

| Code                                 | Branches                           |
| ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------- |
| `if (a) …`, `a ? b : c`              | `a` is truthy, `a` is falsy        |
| `a && b`, `a \|\| b`, `a ?? b`       | `a` is evaluated, `b` is evaluated |
| `switch`                             | Each `case` is entered             |
| `function f(a = 1)`, `{ a = 1 } = b` | The default is used                |
| `a &&= b`, `a \|\|= b`, `a ??= b`    | `b` is evaluated                   |
| `a?.b`                               | `b` is evaluated                   |
| `catch {}` with an empty body        | It is entered                      |

### Differences from Istanbul

Bun reports what [Istanbul](https://istanbul.js.org) reports, which is what Jest, Vitest and `nyc` go by. It also reports code that Istanbul doesn't look at:

- The last three kinds of branches above.
- Every line with code. Istanbul counts the lines on which a statement starts. A closing bracket doesn't cover such a line, or the code before it. A line with only the head of a function is covered when the function is called.
- Private methods as functions, and `class`, `enum`, `namespace` and `export default` as statements.

Methods and arrow functions have names like `Cart.total`. Istanbul calls them `(anonymous_0)`.

### Code That Is Not Measured

- Code that comes from a string: `eval()`, `new Function()`, `node:vm`, `module._compile()`, `data:` and `blob:` URLs
- Code that runs in a subprocess
- Code that runs in a [macro](/bundler/macros) on another thread, which is where most files that you `import` run their macros

Code that runs in a `Worker` is measured.

## Coverage Thresholds

Set a coverage threshold in `bunfig.toml`. If your test suite does not meet or exceed it, `bun test` prints an error and exits with code 1.

```txt
error: Coverage of branches is 75.00%, which is below the threshold of 80%
```

### Simple Threshold

```toml title="bunfig.toml" icon="settings"
[test]
# To require 90% line-level and function-level coverage
coverageThreshold = 0.9
```

### Detailed Thresholds

```toml title="bunfig.toml" icon="settings"
[test]
coverageThreshold = { lines = 0.9, functions = 0.9, statements = 0.9, branches = 0.8 }
```

Bun checks only the keys you set. If `coverageInclude` leaves no file to report, the thresholds are not met.

A negative number is the most that may be left uncovered:

```toml title="bunfig.toml" icon="settings"
[test]
# At most 10 lines are not covered
coverageThreshold = { lines = -10 }
```

### Per-File Thresholds

Bun compares thresholds with the `All files` row. To require them of every file, set `perFile`:

```toml title="bunfig.toml" icon="settings"
[test]
coverageThreshold = { lines = 0.9, functions = 0.9, perFile = true }
```

### Thresholds for Some Files

A key can be a glob pattern, a folder or a file. Its thresholds apply to the matching files together, or to each of them if it sets `perFile`. A key that starts with `!` is for all other files. As in Vitest, the thresholds for all files still include these files. Jest leaves them out.

```toml title="bunfig.toml" icon="settings"
[test.coverageThreshold]
lines = 0.8
"src/billing" = { lines = 1, branches = 1 }
"src/**/*.util.ts" = { functions = 0.9, perFile = true }
```

As in Jest, the key `global` holds the thresholds for all files.

## Coverage Reporters

By default, Bun prints coverage reports to the console.

To save a report for CI or other tools, pass `--coverage-reporter=lcov` on the command line or set `coverageReporter` in `bunfig.toml`.

```toml title="bunfig.toml" icon="settings"
[test]
coverageReporter = ["text", "lcov"]  # default ["text"]
coverageDir = "path/to/somewhere"    # default "coverage"
```

### Available Reporters

| Reporter       | Description                                                               |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `text`         | Prints a table to the console                                             |
| `lcov`         | Writes `lcov.info`                                                        |
| `json`         | Writes `coverage-final.json` in Istanbul's format, with lines and columns |
| `json-summary` | Writes `coverage-summary.json` in Istanbul's format, with totals per file |

### LCOV Coverage Reporter

The lcov reporter writes an `lcov.info` file to the coverage directory.

```toml title="bunfig.toml" icon="settings"
[test]
coverageReporter = "lcov"
```

```bash terminal icon="terminal"
# Or via CLI
bun test --coverage --coverage-reporter=lcov
```

Tools and services that read the LCOV format include:

- **Code editors**: VS Code extensions can show coverage inline
- **CI/CD services**: GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, CircleCI
- **Coverage services**: Codecov, Coveralls
- **IDEs**: WebStorm, IntelliJ IDEA

#### Using LCOV with GitHub Actions

```yaml title=".github/workflows/test.yml" icon="file-code"
name: Test with Coverage
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
      - run: bun install
      - run: bun test --coverage --coverage-reporter=lcov
      - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v3
        with:
          file: ./coverage/lcov.info
```

### HTML Reports

Istanbul's tools read the output of the `json` reporter. To see which part of a line is not covered, generate an HTML report:

```bash terminal icon="terminal"
bun test --coverage-reporter=json --coverage-dir=.nyc_output
bunx nyc report --reporter=html
```

## Excluding Files from Coverage

### Skip Test Files

Coverage reports exclude test files by default. To include them:

```toml title="bunfig.toml" icon="settings"
[test]
coverageSkipTestFiles = false  # default true
```

When `coverageSkipTestFiles` is `true` (the default), the coverage report excludes files matching test patterns (for example `*.test.ts`, `*.spec.js`) and [preload](/test/configuration#preload-scripts) scripts.

### Ignore Specific Paths and Patterns

`coveragePathIgnorePatterns` excludes specific files or file patterns from coverage reports:

```toml title="bunfig.toml" icon="settings"
[test]
# Single pattern
coveragePathIgnorePatterns = "**/*.spec.ts"

# Multiple patterns
coveragePathIgnorePatterns = [
  "**/*.spec.ts",
  "**/*.test.ts",
  "src/utils/**",
  "*.config.js"
]
```

The option accepts glob patterns. Bun excludes files matching any of the patterns from every report.

#### Common Use Cases

```toml title="bunfig.toml" icon="settings"
[test]
coveragePathIgnorePatterns = [
  # Exclude utility files
  "src/utils/**",

  # Exclude configuration files
  "*.config.js",
  "webpack.config.ts",
  "vite.config.ts",

  # Exclude specific test patterns
  "**/*.spec.ts",
  "**/*.e2e.ts",

  # Exclude build artifacts
  "dist/**",
  "build/**",

  # Exclude generated files
  "src/generated/**",
  "**/*.generated.ts",

  # Exclude vendor/third-party code
  "vendor/**",
  "third-party/**"
]
```

## Excluding Code from Coverage

Bun understands the comments of Istanbul, Vitest, c8 and Node.js.

```ts title="config.ts" icon="/icons/typescript.svg"
/* istanbul ignore next */
function debugOnly() {}

/* istanbul ignore else */
if (process.platform === "linux") setup();
```

| Comment                                                               | Leaves out                                                   |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `istanbul ignore next`, `v8 ignore next`                              | The next statement, function, `case`, property or expression |
| `c8 ignore next`, `node:coverage ignore next`                         | The next line                                                |
| `c8 ignore next 3`, `v8 ignore next 3`, `node:coverage ignore next 3` | The next 3 lines                                             |
| `ignore if`                                                           | The first branch of the next `if`                            |
| `ignore else`                                                         | The second branch of the next `if`                           |
| `ignore start` … `ignore stop` or `ignore end`                        | The lines in between                                         |
| `node:coverage disable` … `node:coverage enable`                      | The lines in between                                         |
| `ignore file`                                                         | The file                                                     |

`if`, `else`, `start`, `stop`, `end` and `file` work after `istanbul`, `v8` and `c8`. After code on the same line, `c8 ignore next` leaves out that line.

## Sourcemaps

Bun reports positions in your source files. If a test loads the output of `bun build --target=bun --sourcemap`, Bun reports the files it was built from. The report is about their text at the time of the build. Modules in the namespace of a plugin are not in it. Branches and statements that the bundler removes or merges can be missing from it.

Bun reports the bundle itself if these files are not where the source map says, or if they are in your project and `coverageInclude` matches only the bundle.

If a [plugin](/runtime/plugins) compiles a file, Bun measures the code that `onLoad` returns, and goes by the ignore comments in that code. To get positions in the file, end the code with an inline source map of that file. Lines of the code without a mapping are not in the report.

```ts title="preload.ts" icon="/icons/typescript.svg"
import { plugin } from "bun";
import { compile } from "svelte/compiler";

plugin({
  name: "svelte",
  setup(build) {
    build.onLoad({ filter: /\.svelte$/ }, async ({ path }) => {
      const { js } = compile(await Bun.file(path).text(), { filename: path });
      return { contents: `${js.code}\n//# sourceMappingURL=${js.map.toUrl()}`, loader: "js" };
    });
  },
});
```

Don't edit code after its source map is written. If that moves the code, the report is wrong.

To report the code that runs instead, which is the output of the transpiler or the bundle itself, set `coverageIgnoreSourcemaps` to `true`. You rarely want this outside of debugging.

```toml title="bunfig.toml" icon="settings"
[test]
coverageIgnoreSourcemaps = true  # default false
```

<Warning>
  When using this option, you probably want to stick a `// @bun` comment at the top of the source file to opt out of the
  transpilation process.
</Warning>

## Coverage Defaults

By default, coverage reports:

- **Include** the files that your tests load (choose the files with `coverageInclude`)
- **Exclude** files outside of the working directory (include them with `coverageInclude`)
- **Exclude** `node_modules` directories
- **Exclude** files loaded with non-JS/TS loaders (for example `.css`, `.txt`) unless you specify a custom JS loader
- **Exclude** test files and preload scripts (include them with `coverageSkipTestFiles = false`)
- Can exclude additional files with `coveragePathIgnorePatterns`

## Advanced Configuration

### Custom Coverage Directory

```toml title="bunfig.toml" icon="settings"
[test]
coverageDir = "coverage-reports"  # default "coverage"
```

### Multiple Reporters

```toml title="bunfig.toml" icon="settings"
[test]
coverageReporter = ["text", "lcov"]
```

### Coverage with Specific Test Patterns

```bash terminal icon="terminal"
# Run coverage only on specific test files
bun test --coverage src/components/*.test.ts

# Run coverage with name pattern
bun test --coverage --test-name-pattern="API"
```

## CI/CD Integration

### GitHub Actions Example

```yaml title=".github/workflows/coverage.yml" icon="file-code"
name: Coverage Report
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  coverage:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Bun
        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install

      - name: Run tests with coverage
        run: bun test --coverage --coverage-reporter=lcov

      - name: Upload to Codecov
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v3
        with:
          file: ./coverage/lcov.info
          fail_ci_if_error: true
```

### GitLab CI Example

```yaml title=".gitlab-ci.yml"
test:coverage:
  stage: test
  script:
    - bun install
    - bun test --coverage --coverage-reporter=text --coverage-reporter=lcov
  coverage: '/All files\s*\|\s*[\d.]+\s*\|\s*(\d+\.\d+)/'
  artifacts:
    paths:
      - coverage/lcov.info
```

## Interpreting Coverage Reports

### Text Output Explanation

- **% Funcs**: Percentage of functions that ran
- **% Lines**: Percentage of lines with code that ran
- **% Stmts**: Percentage of statements that ran
- **% Branch**: Percentage of branches that were taken
- **Uncovered Line #s**: The lines that never ran, in red. If every line ran, the lines with a branch, statement or function that didn't, in yellow.
- **All files**: The total over all files. A large file weighs more than a small one.

### What to Aim For

- **80%+ overall coverage**: Generally considered good
- **90%+ critical paths**: Important business logic should be well-tested
- **100% utility functions**: Pure functions and utilities can be tested completely
- **Lower coverage for UI components**: Often acceptable as they may require integration tests

## Best Practices

### Focus on Quality, Not Just Quantity

```ts title="test.ts" icon="/icons/typescript.svg"
// Good: Test actual functionality
test("calculateTax should handle different tax rates", () => {
  expect(calculateTax(100, 0.08)).toBe(8);
  expect(calculateTax(100, 0.1)).toBe(10);
  expect(calculateTax(0, 0.08)).toBe(0);
});

// Avoid: Just hitting lines for coverage
test("calculateTax exists", () => {
  calculateTax(100, 0.08); // No assertions!
});
```

### Test Edge Cases

```ts title="test.ts" icon="/icons/typescript.svg"
test("user input validation", () => {
  // Test normal case
  expect(validateEmail("user@example.com")).toBe(true);

  // Test edge cases that improve coverage meaningfully
  expect(validateEmail("")).toBe(false);
  expect(validateEmail("invalid")).toBe(false);
  expect(validateEmail(null)).toBe(false);
});
```

### Use Coverage to Find Missing Tests

```bash terminal icon="terminal"
# Run coverage to identify untested code
bun test --coverage

# Look at specific files that need attention
bun test --coverage src/critical-module.ts
```

### Combine with Other Quality Metrics

Coverage is only one metric. Also consider:

- **Code review quality**
- **Integration test coverage**
- **Error handling tests**
- **Performance tests**
- **Type safety**

## Troubleshooting

### Coverage Not Showing for Some Files

By default, the report lists only the files in the working directory that your tests load. Set [`coverageInclude`](#report-files-that-no-test-loads) to list the others too.

### False Coverage Reports

If you see coverage reports that don't match your expectations:

1. Check [what counts as covered](#what-counts-as-covered).
2. Verify file patterns in `coverageInclude` and `coveragePathIgnorePatterns`
3. Ensure test files import the code to test

### Performance Issues with Large Codebases

Only files in the report pay for coverage. Exclude the code you don't need coverage for:

```toml title="bunfig.toml" icon="settings"
[test]
# Exclude large directories you don't need coverage for
coveragePathIgnorePatterns = [
  "vendor/**",
  "generated/**"
]
```

Consider running coverage only on CI or specific branches rather than every test run during development.
